verdict.rationale: Homebrew's own Brewfile can be checked into a project repository, and `brew bundle install` installs the declared tools from it, for example running `brew install ruby`. `brew bundle exec` offers a project shell environment. However, nothing documents per-project version pinning or switching between runtime versions, and community users say they still rely on pyenv or nvm for multiple Node or Python versions. missing for 10: per-project version pinning in the Brewfile, switching between multiple installed runtime versions per project, independent hands-on corroboration of per-project runtime management.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install and switch language runtimes or tool versions per project from a checked-in config file

citations.quote: Adding a `Brewfile` to a project's repository (like you might a `package.json`, `Gemfile` or `requirements.txt`) is a nicer way of encoding project dependencies for developer environments.
this will take instructions from the Brewfile to run brew install ruby and install Ruby if needed
Run your shell in a `brew bundle exec` environment.
It allows you to tell users to run a single command to install all dependencies for a project and start any services.
